research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding a pick-and-roll (PNR) in the same possession
play-type labeling from play-by-play (derived possession records)
sequential play-type premiums (X->Y vs Y baseline)
label leakage (assisted flag, foul endings) and outcome-derived labels
methodological_questions: Can a teammate drive and a PNR be identified reliably and in the right order from the play-by-play and derived play-type labels?
Is the pooled effect of a prior teammate drive on PNR PPP distinguishable from selection (which possessions get a drive then PNR), player and lineup quality, and a placebo?
Are there enough drive-then-PNR possessions to power a pooled test, given that earlier per-player-pair cells were small (n=30-70)?
How should multiplicity, season drift and the regular-season/playoff split be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive player and teammate sequence premiums. Positive DRIVE->PNR cells appeared (L. Doncic same-player +0.309, n=53; J. Brown->J. Tatum teammate +0.326, n=43). D. Bane DRIVE->PNR was -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7). Signs were mixed on the same pair across players. Most cells were n<50 and directional, with no multiplicity correction. The record states that Brown->Tatum was later shown to be a placebo artifact (APPS-070). Its recorded risks include label error, placebo dependence, small sample and drift.

Play-type label audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% vs a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw rate 1.7% vs a 14-22% benchmark, and foul possessions leaking into OTHER. The record says the labels have systematic issues that undermine adaptation findings.

Label backfill verification FAIL: PNR share 28.7% vs a 20-28% band, 3100 games with team PNR share >33%, team identity checks failed, and 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. PNR PPP of 0.948 passed.
Labeling audit: OTHER PPP inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark, PNR 22% foul rate, and only 0.7% of 50,668 possessions mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.
The assisted flag exists only on makes, which produced SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP (100% makes) until the play-type inferrer was rewritten. This is an outcome-derived label leak.
2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots varies by team from 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND). PNR rates were used as a calibration input for the proxy PNR classifier, with no pass/fail gate.
Defensive PPP allowed, RS vs playoffs: PNR share jumped +12.1pp, which may reflect tagging differences. The record carries LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks.

Team-level DRIVE PPP was 1.198 in the regular season vs 0.912 in the playoffs, and PNR PPP was 0.173 lower in the playoffs. No CIs. This is a regular-season/playoff level shift in the relevant play types.
PPP changes across playoff series buckets (PNR +0.087) with selection and regression-to-the-mean caveats and no CIs.
On-ball coverage labels reached only 14.9% and 3.3% confident labeling, and switches_on was unpopulated in the NBA matchups feed. Defensive scheme cannot be used as a control from this feed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Per-player-pair DRIVE->PNR premium cells with min n=30, flagged at |t|>=2 with no multiplicity correction
failed_approaches.why: Small samples, mixed signs, no multiplicity control, and a flagged top result (Brown->Tatum +0.326) was later shown to be a placebo artifact per the record's note.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label backfill using proxy-calibrated PNR labels
failed_approaches.why: Verification FAIL on PNR share, team identity and per-game PNR share; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Possession-level PPP by inferred play type using the assisted flag
failed_approaches.why: The assisted flag exists only on makes, creating an outcome-derived label and an artifactual 2.83 PPP.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing play-type PPP as real efficiency differences
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending leakage inflated OTHER and deflated DRIVE, and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverage from matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Label rates of 3-15% and an unpopulated switches_on field.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests the pooled claim that a teammate DRIVE before a PNR raises PNR PPP. The only related work (FAM:SF40) is descriptive, with no multiplicity correction.

The recorded sequence results are heterogeneous in sign across players and pairs, so a universal 'any drive raises PPP' reading has recorded counter-instances (D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324, n=70, t=-2.7).
One recorded positive teammate DRIVE->PNR cell (Brown->Tatum) was later shown to be a placebo artifact, per the record's note.
Play-type labels for DRIVE and PNR in this pipeline have recorded quality failures (proxy-calibrated PNR labels, foul leakage, outcome-derived flags).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the pooled average effect of a prior teammate drive on PNR PPP is positive, zero or negative.
How many same-possession drive-then-PNR events exist across 2022-26 and whether a pooled test is powered.

Whether the recorded sequence premiums reflect the same-possession ordering the question requires. SF40 describes 'same initiator on t and t+2' and does not state that the sequence is within one possession.
Whether any effect is causal rather than selection on possession context, lineup or ball-handler.
Anything about the 2025-26 playoffs, which are not complete as of the question date.
own_inferences: 'Any' is read as a pooled average effect, since a universal claim is falsified by any negative cell and the Bane cell already points that way. The testable version is the pooled mean difference plus its heterogeneity.

A DRIVE followed by a PNR in the same possession implies the drive did not end the possession (kick-out or reset). Conditioning on that is a selection on drive outcome, and the comparison group should be possessions with comparable earlier non-drive actions or elapsed time.
If PNR labels are partly proxy-calibrated with PBP-derived context, a DRIVE just before a PNR could shape the PNR label or its PPP mechanically, creating an artifact in either direction.

Given the recorded artifact history in this pipeline (assisted-flag leak, foul leakage, placebo failure of the top cell), the most likely 'finding' from a naive run is a spurious or label-driven premium.
uncertainties: The count of exposed possessions is unknown. A gate is needed before any inference.
Whether the derived graph records preserve within-possession event order and clock, and whether DRIVE labels are independent of subsequent outcomes.
Whether the current labeler version fixed the recorded leaks (SF-PAP-096 reports a rewrite but later audits still show FAIL).
The 'preceding' window (immediately prior action vs anywhere earlier in the possession) is not defined in the question.
The effect of the label-quality failures on 2022-23 to 2025-26 differs by season, which is not retrievable here.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have proceeded with a pooled regression. The records changed the decision to proceed_with_changes: they show the likely top cell was a placebo artifact, per-pair cells were underpowered with no multiplicity control, signs were mixed, and PNR/DRIVE labels have recorded leakage and proxy-calibration problems. The design therefore adds a label-validity gate, an exposure-count gate, placebo tests, a pooled estimand with pre-specified heterogeneity analysis, and a holdout split.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR and DRIVE labels have recorded audit FAILs (82.8% proxy_calibrated PNR labels, foul leakage). The test is not valid until the label-validity gate passes.

The number of same-possession teammate-drive-then-PNR events is unknown. Earlier per-pair cells were n=30-70. A pooled test is feasible only if the exposed count reaches the roughly 2,000-7,500 per arm needed for 0.05-0.10 PPP effects.
The one recorded positive teammate DRIVE->PNR cell (Brown->Tatum) was shown to be a placebo artifact. Any positive result must survive placebo and permutation tests.

prior_work.summary: No pooled test of the stated claim was retrieved. FAM:SF40 gives descriptive per-pair premiums (mixed signs, one cell later labelled a placebo artifact, no multiplicity correction). The labeling-audit families show that the PNR and DRIVE labels this question depends on have recorded quality problems. The question is not answered.

risks.text: PNR labels are largely proxy-calibrated and DRIVE/PNR distributions fail audits. Misclassified DRIVE or PNR events contaminate both exposure and outcome.
Labels built from makes, assisted flags or foul endings (the recorded SPOT_UP and OTHER leaks) can tie the exposure or the PNR label to the outcome.
Exposure must be defined using only events before PNR initiation. Labels that use later events in the possession leak the outcome into the exposure.

Drives happen with specific ball handlers, lineups, shot-clock states and opponent coverages, and the possession surviving the drive is selected. These drive both the likelihood of a PNR afterwards and its PPP.
Drive-then-PNR events may be rare, especially within player pairs and after restriction to within-possession order with a short window.
PNR possession outcomes have SD about 1.1 PPP. Detecting 0.05 PPP needs roughly 7,500 per arm and 0.10 needs roughly 1,900 (own estimate). Cluster dependence within games and teams raises these.
A recorded positive teammate cell was a placebo artifact. Results need placebo exposures to remain null.
Per-player and per-pair cells previously flagged at |t|>=2 without correction. Heterogeneity analyses must be pre-specified and corrected.
Labeler versions, league PNR rates and regular-season vs playoff PPP differ (PNR -0.173 in playoffs per the record), so pooling across seasons or game types can confound the estimate.
Foul and free-throw outcomes and possession-ending rules can set mechanical bounds on PPP differences for drive-related sequences.

design.estimand: Average difference in PPP of the PNR action (points scored from PNR initiation to end of possession, free throws included) between PNR possessions where a teammate of the PNR ball handler, other than the PNR ball handler and screener, recorded a DRIVE earlier in the same possession within a pre-specified window (primary: within the preceding 8 seconds of game clock, secondary: any earlier action), and matched PNR possessions without such a drive. Also report the sign distribution of effects across initiators as a heterogeneity check. 'Any' is operationalized as the pooled average plus the share of pre-registered strata with negative point estimates, and the claim is read as the pooled average effect.
design.unit: PNR possession (one row per possession with a PNR), clustered by game and by offensive team-season.
design.sample: Discovery: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs. Confirmation: 2025-26 regular season, which is complete from 2026-04-13. 2025-26 playoffs are not complete on the question date and are excluded from any decision. Reserve them as a pre-declared out-of-sample holdout once complete (from 2026-06-21). Playoffs and regular season are analysed separately with no pooling. Exclude garbage time, end-of-period possessions, possessions beginning with a shooting foul, and transition possessions. Include only possessions where the PNR label comes from event-level evidence (not proxy_calibrated).
design.power: Gate 0: report counts of exposed and unexposed PNR possessions per season and game type before looking at PPP. Proceed to inference only if exposed n >= 2,000 per arm in discovery (detects about 0.10 PPP at 80% power with SD about 1.1, ignoring clustering). Use the design-effect inflation from game and team clustering. If n is between 2,000 and 7,500, label results as only able to rule out effects larger than about 0.10 PPP. If n < 2,000, declare the question untestable at useful power and stop. Do not run per-player-pair analyses unless n >= 200 per cell.
design.controls: Label-validity gate first: manually audit a random sample of at least 300 exposed and 300 unexposed possessions against play-by-play for DRIVE and PNR correctness (target precision >= 0.85) and confirm the exposure uses only pre-PNR events and no assisted or foul flags. Then use a regression or matched design controlling for ball handler and screener identity (fixed effects), lineup quality proxies, opponent team, score margin, period, shot-clock or elapsed possession time at PNR start, home/away, season, and whether the earlier event was a kick-out vs reset. Compare against a control exposure of non-drive early actions (e.g., a dribble handoff or non-drive touch of equal elapsed time) to separate the drive from simply having more elapsed possession. Exclude the drive's own points (possession-ending drives are not in the sample).
design.falsification: (1) Placebo exposures: assign the DRIVE flag to a random possession event in the same team-game (shuffle) and to a pre-specified non-drive action type; the effect should be null. (2) Time-shifted placebo: define 'drive' as a drive occurring after the PNR within the same possession, which cannot cause the PNR outcome. (3) Replicate the pooled estimate with the earlier-flagged Brown->Tatum style pair excluded to test dependence on a single pair. (4) Re-run on labels from an independent labeler version or on a hand-audited subsample. A positive pooled estimate that also appears under placebo or time-shift is classified as artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary pooled test (two-sided, alpha=0.05). Secondary: up to 6 pre-specified strata (season x game type, and the two window definitions), controlled with Holm correction. Any per-player or per-pair analysis is exploratory, labelled as such, and uses Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.10 with a stated total number of tests.
design.decision_rule: Supported: label gate passes, Gate 0 passes, primary effect > 0 with 95% cluster-robust CI excluding 0 and a lower bound of at least +0.03 PPP, placebo and time-shift effects are null (CI includes 0 and are smaller in magnitude), and the confirmation season replicates sign and at least half the effect size. Rejected: adequately powered and the 95% CI lies within +/-0.03 PPP, with placebo null. Artifact: placebo or time-shift effects comparable to the main effect, or the effect vanishes after removing proxy-calibrated labels. Untestable or stop: label gate fails (<0.85 precision) or Gate 0 fails. Otherwise report as inconclusive. A claim of 'any' (universal) is not supported if the heterogeneity analysis shows negative effects in a pre-specified stratum with a CI excluding 0.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived graph possession records for 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons plus 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoffs, frozen as of the registration date (2026-06-14) with the labeler commit hash and label-quality audit output recorded. 2025-26 regular season is complete (from 2026-04-13). 2025-26 playoffs are partial on the registration date and are reserved as a holdout once complete (from 2026-06-21).

methodological_questions: Can a drive preceding a PNR be identified reliably from play-by-play event data and derived play-type labels?
Does a prior teammate drive causally raise PNR PPP after controlling for lineup, ball-handler, screener, defense and game context?
How should sequence ordering, possession windows and label definitions be set to avoid lookahead leakage and outcome-derived labels?
Is there enough exposure of drive-then-PNR possessions to power a test, and how should multiple comparisons and drift across seasons be handled?

You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.

I'm checking whether the claim that any teammate's drive before a pick-and-roll raises that play's PPP can be overturned by one counterexample, since "any" makes it universal. The pooled figure only gives an average effect, and the per-player results vary, with Bane's drive-to-PNR effect coming out negative. I also need to account for the playoff dates, which only partly overlap with the question's timing.

I'm settling on proceeding with changes and giving rough odds to each outcome, with about 40% on the claim being testable. The design needs a pre-registered split: 2022–25 for discovery, the 2025–26 regular season for confirmation, and the playoffs held out, since they only become available after the question date. I also need to guard against label errors, outcome-derived labels, selection effects from drives happening when the offense already has an advantage, and unclear definitions of "preceding," along with multiple testing.

I'm now setting the design in more detail: the estimand compares PNRs preceded by a teammate's drive within the same possession against matched PNRs without one, using only information available before the PNR starts. I'm treating the points scored from the PNR onward as the outcome, since a drive that ended in a shot would have ended the possession, so a PNR afterward means the drive was a non-scoring kick-out.
